newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Ergobank says 96 profit up 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek Ergobank says 96 profit up 20 pct.

text.p: Greece's Ergobank said its fiscal 1996 profit rose 20 percent to 44.8 billion drachmas from 37.4 billion a year earlier.
The bank's board will propose to the upcoming annual shareholders meeting in May 27 a dividend per share of 950 drachmas, up 17 percent from 1995.
Ergobank president Xenophon Nikitas told the bank's board that return on equity (ROE) reached 60.7 percent based on 1996 financial results.
The bank's equity capital reached 71.4 billion drachmas at the close of 1996 and will rise to 100 billion after completion of its ongoing rights issue.
Gross profit also rose 20 percent to 76.7 billion drachmas, Ergobank said.

"The fact that the growth rate of net and gross profit is the same despite the expansion of the branch network and higher operational expenses proves how prudent and profitable was the bank's treasury management," it said.
Ergobank's total assets reached 1.11 trillion drachmas at year-end 1996.
Its shares closed up 310 drachmas at 15,400 for a gain of 2.05 percent.
